heading: A worked example: one number, several explanations
exactSourceText: Suppose pathology estimates **50% purity**: half the cells in the sample are cancer cells. Under a simple model in which each affected cancer cell has two copies of the region and one altered copy, expected VAF = purity × cancer-cell fraction ÷ 2. Solving, 0.20 = 0.50 × CCF ÷ 2 gives a cancer-cell fraction of about **80%**. The same 20% VAF in a sample of pure cancer cells would fit only about 40%. Copy-number gains or losses change the arithmetic again, so this is a worked illustration, not an estimate for a real sample.

heading: From model to person: the safety test
exactSourceText: IACS-010759 then entered two phase 1 trials, in acute myeloid leukemia (17 people) and advanced solid tumors (23 people). It had a narrow therapeutic window: dose-limiting rises in blood lactate and nerve toxicity prevented the dose needed to keep the target blocked. Only modest target inhibition and limited antitumor activity were seen, no recommended phase 2 dose was set, and both trials were discontinued [4]. Normal tissues also respire, so an energy dependence in a tumor model has to clear a toxicity test that a culture cannot run.
